body_html:
The best Spanish podcasts for learners are the ones that match two things: your level and the accent you want to understand. A podcast that is perfect for a beginner learning Mexican Spanish can be frustrating for someone heading to Madrid, and vice versa. I have listened to every podcast on this list, many of them on long walks while I was learning, and I still recommend them today. Here they are, organized by level, with a note on the accent each one uses.

Quick answer
  • Best for beginners: Coffee Break Spanish and the Duolingo Spanish Podcast
  • Best for Mexican Spanish: Learn Spanish and Go
  • Best for intermediate learners: Españolistos and Notes in Spanish
  • Best daily habit: Hoy Hablamos
  • Best for advanced learners: Radio Ambulante
{{toc}}

Best Spanish podcasts for beginners

1. Coffee Break Spanish

Best for: your first steps, with clear explanations in English  ·  Level: A1–B1

Coffee Break Spanish works like a short class: a teacher and a learner go through each lesson together, mixing English explanations with Spanish practice. Episodes are about 20 minutes, the length of a coffee break, and the structure makes it feel like a real course. It is where many people, including me, first got used to hearing Spanish regularly. Coffee Break Languages

Accent: mostly Spain, with other varieties in later seasons.

2. Duolingo Spanish Podcast

Best for: beginners who want stories, not lessons  ·  Level: A2–B1

Each episode tells a true story in easy Spanish, with a narrator stepping in, in English, to fill the gaps. You follow because you want to know what happens next, and the Spanish comes along for the ride. It is the podcast I recommend to people who find lesson podcasts boring.

Accent: varied, mostly Latin American storytellers.

3. Learn Spanish and Go

Best for: learners interested in Mexican Spanish and culture  ·  Level: A2–B1

Made by a couple living in Mexico, this podcast focuses on everyday Mexican Spanish, slang and culture, often explained in a relaxed conversation. If your partner, family or coworkers are Mexican, this is one of the most useful podcasts you can listen to. It pairs well with my guide to {{link:mexican-slang|Mexican slang}}.

Accent: Mexico.

{{image:2}}

Best Spanish podcasts for intermediate learners

4. Españolistos

Best for: moving from learner Spanish to real conversation  ·  Level: B1–B2

Hosted by Andrea, from Colombia, and Nate, from the United States, Españolistos is almost entirely in Spanish but spoken slowly and clearly, about everyday topics. It is the bridge I recommend between beginner podcasts and native-speed Spanish. Their banter is part of the charm.

Accent: Colombia, with a learner’s perspective from the US.

5. Notes in Spanish

Best for: hearing how people really talk in Spain  ·  Level: B1–C1

Ben and Marina, a couple based in Madrid, record natural conversations about life in Spain, with levels from intermediate to advanced. Because the conversations are unscripted, you hear real fillers, interruptions and expressions, the kind I cover in {{link:spanish-filler-words|Spanish filler words}} and {{link:spain-slang|Spain slang}}.

Accent: Spain.

6. Hoy Hablamos

Best for: a daily listening habit  ·  Level: B1–C1

A short episode almost every day, entirely in Spanish, on culture, language and current topics. The daily rhythm is what makes it valuable: ten or fifteen minutes with your morning coffee adds up quickly.

Accent: Spain.

7. News in Slow Spanish

Best for: following current events at your level  ·  Level: B1–B2

Real news, read and discussed at a slower pace, with transcripts and grammar notes. It is a good way to learn the vocabulary of the news without being overwhelmed. There are editions for both Spain and Latin America. News in Slow Spanish

Accent: your choice of Spain or Latin America.

Best Spanish podcast for advanced learners

8. Radio Ambulante

Best for: long, beautifully produced stories from Latin America  ·  Level: B2–C2

Radio Ambulante, distributed by NPR, tells long-form stories from across Latin America, with real voices and real accents from many countries. It is not made for learners, which is exactly why it is so good once you are ready. When I want to hear how Spanish sounds in different countries, this is what I listen to. Radio Ambulante

Accent: many Latin American countries.

{{image:3}}

How to learn from podcasts, not just listen

  1. Choose the right level. If you understand less than about 70% of an episode, go down a level; if you understand everything easily, go up.
  2. Listen twice. Once for the general idea, once to catch details. Use the transcript the second time if there is one.
  3. Pause and repeat. Shadow a sentence out loud, copying the rhythm. It does wonders for pronunciation.
  4. Save phrases. Write down one useful expression per episode and use it that week. This is the habit I describe in {{link:sentence-mining-spanish|sentence mining}}.
  5. Mix accents gradually. Start with the accent you need most, then add others; see {{link:latin-american-vs-spain-spanish|Latin American vs Spain Spanish}}.

Podcasts and other tools

Podcasts are the best way to fit Spanish into time you already have: commutes, walks, chores. They are not enough on their own, though. Combine them with a little reading and speaking: my list of the {{link:best-books-to-learn-spanish|best books to learn Spanish}} covers reading, and the {{link:best-apps-to-learn-spanish|best apps to learn Spanish}} include tools for speaking with tutors. If listening is your weakest skill, also look at comprehensible input video, which I explain in {{link:comprehensible-input-spanish|comprehensible input for Spanish}}.

Final thoughts

The best Spanish podcasts are the ones you look forward to. Pick one at your level and in the accent you need, listen a little every day, and move up when it starts to feel easy. Your ear will change faster than you expect.

faq.q: What is the best Spanish podcast for beginners?
faq.a: Coffee Break Spanish for structured lessons, and the Duolingo Spanish Podcast for easy stories.

faq.q: Which Spanish podcast is best for Mexican Spanish?
faq.a: Learn Spanish and Go focuses on Mexican Spanish and culture.

faq.q: Can I learn Spanish just by listening to podcasts?
faq.a: Podcasts are excellent for listening, but you also need some reading, vocabulary work and speaking practice.

faq.q: What Spanish podcast should advanced learners listen to?
faq.a: Radio Ambulante, a long-form storytelling podcast from Latin America distributed by NPR.

faq.q: How often should I listen to Spanish podcasts?
faq.a: A little every day works best. Fifteen minutes daily beats two hours once a week.
